result.summary: Avoid reusing cached validation state across calls in the libbitcoinkernel C API. `btck_block_check` and `btck_chainstate_manager_process_block` now operate on a shallow copy of the block without cached flags (`fChecked`, `m_checked_merkle_root`, `m_checked_witness_commitment`), while still sharing the transaction vector pointers.
result.problem: A `btck_Block` wraps a shared `CBlock`. Once validation succeeds under one set of consensus parameters, `CheckBlock` sets `fChecked` on the underlying object, causing any subsequent validation of that block under different parameters or flags to return true without re-verifying rules such as signet challenge solutions or proof-of-work.
evidence: PR description: 'a regtest block fails btck_block_check with mainnet params and ALL flags. After it has been checked once with regtest params, the same call with mainnet params returns 1.'

PR description: 'a signet block that satisfies an OP_TRUE challenge but not an OP_RETURN one: processing it on a chainstate manager with the OP_TRUE challenge first, then on a second one with the OP_RETURN challenge, connects it on both.'
result.scope_notes: Small fix localized to libbitcoinkernel validation wrappers, along with two unit test cases.
result.card: Prevents cached block validation flags from persisting across different consensus parameters in the libbitcoinkernel C API. Because `btck_Block` wraps a shared block instance, running block validation sets `fChecked` on the underlying object, causing later checks against different chain parameters (such as testing a regtest block against mainnet rules or processing blocks across different signet challenges) to erroneously pass. The PR makes `btck_block_check` and `btck_chainstate_manager_process_block` validate against an unfagged shallow copy of the block sharing transaction pointers.

risk.why: Touches only libbitcoinkernel C wrapper functions and does not affect bitcoind node validation.
